goal: Hook: a circle game with a talking object and the question of how we take turns and ask for help; name and model the talk turn card, "eyes look, wait my turn", and "Can you help me?" with the school helpers by picture (teacher, office, nurse).
note: Start-of-year check (STANDARD section 3), the last ten minutes after the hook: the teacher watches the circle game (can the child name a classmate and take a turn) and marks the class sheet; no separate test, no score. Circle game: a cleared floor, walking feet. ELA lean: ela:ek-discussion runs in the same weeks (ELA K unit 1), one set of talk rules. Disclosure: health's steps (docs/courses/health/APPROACH.md, "If a student tells you something"): the school's reporting route and the counselor.

goal: Pairs and the circle rehearse the two talk turn steps with the talking object, and "Can you help me?" with a puppet stuck on a zipper, until quick.
note: Two hand puppets or paper-bag puppets; cleared circle, walking feet.

goal: On a new scene card (a lost lunch box, a scraped knee), pairs pick the helper picture to ask and say "Can you help me?", and the class uses the talk turn card in a circle about a new class job.

From an invented character's model page, model an "all about me" picture (things I like, one group I belong to: our class), "ask to play" with a puppet, and "I saw you ___" for one thing a classmate did.
note: Families of every kind in the model pages (two moms, two dads, one parent, grandparents, foster families); a child may draw a made-up page; no family or culture asked about by name. No child names who their friends are. Sensitivity read: early childhood guidance on families in the classroom.

goal: Pairs rehearse "ask to play" with a puppet and then a partner, children draw their "all about me" page, and the closing circle practices "I saw you ___".
note: The page may be made up; it is never collected or marked for content.

goal: At free play each child uses "ask to play" with a partner, and the closing circle says "I saw you ___"; the teacher marks the first pairs on "ask to play" from an unseen scene card.
note: End-of-unit evidence begins: the watched rehearsal from an unseen card, pairs not yet seen go first on day 7.

goal: End of unit: a pictured page read aloud, one prompt per sub-skill (circle the child who waits; circle the helper to ask; circle the group the character belongs to; pick the words for asking to play; pick what to say when you saw a classmate help), and the unseen-card "ask to play" rehearsal for pairs not yet seen.
note: The class sheet marks a step "seen" or "not yet", never a rating of the child; thrown away at the end of the unit.

goal: Reteach the step most marked "not yet" in small groups from the class sheet and rehearse it again; the rest rehearse in pairs from the step card; send the family note (pass a spoon as the talking object at a meal).
note: Carry it out: "eyes look, wait my turn" at every class circle. Family note in English and Spanish.

goal: Hook: a picture story and the question of how we can tell what a feeling is; name four feelings from faces on the feelings faces chart, a character's feeling with one clue, and "___ feels ___ because ___".
note: ELA lean ela:ek-story-elements: ELA K unit 2 opens in week 7, so in weeks 5 and 6 the teacher names the character before asking for the feeling (frame bridge). Feelings are named for characters; no child is asked how they feel. No clinical words.

goal: The feelings-faces matching game in small groups: match the face, say the clue, and say "___ feels ___ because ___" for a picture.
On a new picture story, pairs name each character's feeling, point to the clue and give one cause.

Name and model the two calm-down steps, "stop, breathe" (the slow balloon breath), as a body routine, then a puppet with a big mad feeling who stops before grabbing: the feeling is fine and the action is chosen.
note: From today every session opens with the calm-down routine (about 4 minutes with the retrieval item). A plain body skill, no religious or spiritual framing, no clinical words. Disclosure: health's steps (docs/courses/health/APPROACH.md, "If a student tells you something"): the school's reporting route and the counselor.

goal: The class and small groups rehearse "stop, breathe" on the card's cue until quick, then rehearse the puppet's stop before grabbing with a partner.
On a new scene card (a tower knocked over), pairs show "stop, breathe" for the character and pick a chosen action from two pictures.
note: Carry it out from here: "stop, breathe" before line-up and after recess.

goal: Model starting a small task on one signal in a "ready, go" game, and a two-picture "first, next" tidy routine for one center.
note: Candidate kept: group 3's two Understanding sessions split SM6 and SM5 (today), then SM3 and SM7 (day 16), two sub-skills in each (Inside the 20 minutes).

goal: Model finishing one short task to the end of a sand timer with "eyes on my work", and "I choose ___" for a class job, ending in a picture vote on one class choice.
note: Six sand timers, reused by the band; the timer is a pace cue only, never a race. Student voice: the class choice. Library places AASL.V.D.1 with SM3; grade 2 owns it.

goal: Small groups rehearse "ready, go", the "first, next" tidy routine and "eyes on my work" with a sand timer, and each child says "I choose ___" for a choice-time activity.
note: Sand timers as a pace cue only.

goal: In a real center time the class starts on the signal, works to the timer, tidies with "first, next" and takes its picture vote; the teacher watches small groups do both calm-down steps on the card.
note: End-of-unit evidence begins: both calm-down steps on the card, watched in small groups; groups not yet seen go first on day 19.

goal: End of unit: a pictured page read aloud, one prompt per sub-skill (name the character's feeling and the clue; finish "feels ___ because ___"; circle the stop step; pick the chosen action; pick the ready picture; pick the tidy picture; pick the keep-going picture; pick the "I choose" picture), and the calm-down steps for small groups not yet seen.
skills: k-sa-name-feelings; k-sa-feel-think-link; k-sm-calm-down; k-sm-big-feelings; k-sm-step-forward; k-sm-plan-and-tidy; k-sm-stay-on-task; k-sm-have-a-say
note: Feelings in the page are a character's, never the child's own.

goal: Reteach the step most marked "not yet" in at most four small groups and rehearse it again; send the family note (the balloon breath at bedtime, practiced when calm).
skills: k-sa-name-feelings; k-sa-feel-think-link; k-sm-calm-down; k-sm-big-feelings; k-sm-step-forward; k-sm-plan-and-tidy; k-sm-stay-on-task; k-sm-have-a-say
note: Keep the calm-down column of the unit sheet until the mid-year check's respond day (day 22), then throw it away with the check sheet.

goal: Kindergarten mid-year check: unit 1 on new cases, a turn taken in a circle with the talking object, a helper chosen on a pictured page and "ask to play" said for a pictured case, one pictured page read aloud and one watched rehearsal per pair.
note: Draws on unit 1, not unit 2, which its own end-of-unit assessment sampled on days 18 and 19. The frame's calm-down item is not collected again: the unit 2 record of both steps done on the card (days 18 and 19, within ten school days, same task form) stands for it (collect once). The check's sheet is kept only until day 22. Answer-key agent read.

goal: Mid-year respond: reteach the step most marked "not yet" on the check sheet and rehearse it again in pairs; then throw the check sheet away.

Hook: the question of what I can do now; model one thing an invented character is good at on a strengths page, a private "I like" page, and a story where a character breaks a cup and picks the true action from two pictures, saying what it costs.
note: Opening: the calm-down routine as retrieval. Strengths from home languages and culture welcome when offered, never asked about. SA4 checked on the invented case only, never on a child's own conduct. Private pages stay with the child. Disclosure: health's steps (docs/courses/health/APPROACH.md, "If a student tells you something"): the school's reporting route and the counselor. Core link: social-studies:ssk-story-characters (characters in read-alouds who are fair, caring or responsible); the cup story's character is read the same way.

goal: Children draw their own strengths page if they choose and their private "I like" page, and pairs rehearse picking the true action and its cost on two more story cards.
note: Candidate kept: the private page's "steps followed" look-for (chose and drew) is a column on the class sheet; its content is never recorded.

goal: On a new story card (a spilled paint pot), pairs choose the true action and say its cost, and name one thing the character is good at.

Model "I can try" for a character on a new climb, with one step and one person to ask, and a character who practiced hopping, got help and then could; the class tries a clapping pattern for the first of three tries.
note: Growth is practice and help, never belief alone. The keep-going step ("eyes on my work") returns in the opening. Library places AASL.V.D.2 with SA8; grade 2 owns it.

goal: Pairs rehearse "I can try, then ask" on two picture cases, and the class tries the clapping pattern twice more and says how it got easier.
note: Candidate kept: the three clapping tries are timed inside the unit, one on day 26 and two today (about 5 minutes), 0 days added.

goal: At work time each child uses "I can try, then ask" on a new hard task card, and the teacher marks the first pairs saying one step and one helper for an unseen character card.

End of unit: a pictured page read aloud on invented cases, one prompt per sub-skill (the true action and its cost; one step and one helper for a hard thing; what the character is good at; circle the page that shows choosing what to learn), and the clapping pattern tried again, said as "practice made it easier".
note: The course never records a child's own answer to SA7 or SA9.

goal: Reteach the step most marked "not yet" and rehearse it again; send the family note (try a new small skill three times together).
note: Carry it out: "I can try, then ask" at work time.

goal: Hook: the question of how we can tell how someone else feels; model reading a feeling from face and body clues in drawn pictures ("what is the clue?"), "___ wants ___" for two story characters, and "are you OK?" or get a grown-up for a hurt that can be seen, with a puppet.
note: Opening: the feelings faces chart from unit 2 as retrieval. Pictures show children of many backgrounds. Leave-out bridge: if unit 2 was left out, the first ten minutes teach the feelings faces and "stop, breathe" in their one-step form and claim none of unit 2's sub-skills. Disclosure: health's steps (docs/courses/health/APPROACH.md, "If a student tells you something"): the school's reporting route and the counselor.

goal: The "what is the clue?" game in small groups, then pairs rehearse "are you OK?" with the puppet and say what each story character wants.
On a new picture case (a child who dropped a tray), pairs read the feeling and its clue, say what each child wants and act one caring action with the puppet.
note: Carry it out: "what is the clue?" in read-aloud time.

goal: Model "Thank you for ___" for one thing a helper did, "ask, don't guess" when a character guesses a new child cannot play tag, and one class rule from the poster and what it helps people do.
note: Thanks name an action, never a gift or what a family can afford. SA6: the wrong guess rests on a neutral trait (new to the class, glasses), never on skin, hair, dress, faith or speech; checking one's own guess, never blame of a group. Social studies lean ssk-rules-why (social studies K unit 1) is taught before.

goal: Pairs rehearse "ask, don't guess" on two picture cases and "Thank you for ___", and the class acts one rule from the poster.
note: Candidate kept: the drawn picture set is checked for range and for no group shown as the one who guesses wrong (unit plan and sensitivity read, 0 days).

goal: The class makes a thank-you picture for a school helper, naming the act; pairs use "ask, don't guess" on a new card, and the teacher marks the first pairs acting a caring action from an unseen card.

End of unit: a pictured page read aloud, one prompt per sub-skill (the feeling and its clue; what each child wants; the caring action; the thank-you words; the asking action; what a rule helps people do), and the caring action with a puppet from an unseen card for pairs not yet seen.
skills: k-soc-read-feelings; k-soc-their-view; k-soc-care-when-struggle; k-soc-thankful; k-sa-snap-judgments; k-soc-why-rules

goal: Reteach the step most marked "not yet" and rehearse it again; send the family note (find a feeling clue in a picture book at home).

goal: Hook: the question of how we play so everyone can join and stays safe; model a block tower built with "take turns" from the talk turn card, what a good leader (goes slow, looks back) and follower (watches) do, and place pictures (library, playground, lunch) sorted by what each asks.
note: Opening: the talk turn card, "eyes look, wait my turn", as retrieval. Leave-out bridges: if unit 1 was left out, the first ten minutes teach the talk turn card's one-step form; if unit 2 was, the calm-down steps' one-step form; neither claims the left-out unit's sub-skills. Library places AASL.III.D.2 with RS4; grade 2 owns it.

goal: Pairs rehearse the turn-taking tower and the class plays "follow the leader", each child leading once, then acts the right voice for each place picture.
note: Movement: a cleared floor, walking feet, soft shoes, no pushing. Safety read: movement game.

goal: On new place cards (the bus line, a quiet reading corner), pairs act the fitting voice, and small groups build a tower with turns and a named leader.

Model two puppets who want the same ball: "stop, breathe", then "say what you want", and a fair end (take turns, swap or share); then "No, I don't want to" and a walk to a grown-up when the teacher's puppet urges climbing the fence.
note: The teacher (or a teacher-held puppet) voices every pressure, dare, push or unkind line; no child plays the pushing, unkind or upset part. RS6: health owns body safety; the grown-ups named match health K unit 4's trusted helpers, taught in the same weeks (Candidate kept, words checked in the unit plan). Disclosure: health's steps (docs/courses/health/APPROACH.md, "If a student tells you something"): the school's reporting route and the counselor.

goal: Pairs rehearse "stop, breathe, say what you want" with two puppets and pick a fair end, the teacher voicing the upset puppet to the class and each pair answering it in turn.
note: The teacher (or a teacher-held puppet) voices every pressure, dare, push or unkind line; no child plays the pushing, unkind or upset part. Pair rehearsal: the teacher voices that line to the whole class and pairs answer it in turn; the partner is the coach, holding the step card and pointing to each step as it is done. Where two children simply want different things, the partner may play that side from a scripted, calm line, never upset, unkind or pushing.

goal: The second rehearsal session: pairs rehearse "No, I don't want to" and the walk to a grown-up against the teacher's puppet, then run the ball scene again until quick.
note: The twelfth session of the unit (frame). The teacher (or a teacher-held puppet) voices every pressure, dare, push or unkind line; no child plays the pushing, unkind or upset part. Pair rehearsal: the teacher voices that line to the whole class and pairs answer it in turn; the partner is the coach, holding the step card and pointing to each step as it is done. Where two children simply want different things, the partner may play that side from a scripted, calm line, never upset, unkind or pushing.

goal: On new two-puppet cards (one swing, one marker), pairs use the steps and agree a fair end, and say the refusal and the walk for a new pressure card.
note: The teacher (or a teacher-held puppet) voices every pressure, dare, push or unkind line; no child plays the pushing, unkind or upset part. Pair rehearsal: the teacher voices that line to the whole class and pairs answer it in turn; the partner is the coach, holding the step card and pointing to each step as it is done. Where two children simply want different things, the partner may play that side from a scripted, calm line, never upset, unkind or pushing.

goal: Model "stand with them, tell a grown-up" for a puppet left out of a game, a story rule, "only kids with red shirts", called unfair and replaced by an "everyone can join" rule for one center, and Ampe, a clapping and jumping game children play in Ghana, shown on its page.
note: The teacher (or a teacher-held puppet) voices every pressure, dare, push or unkind line; no child plays the pushing, unkind or upset part. SO6 is playground fairness only, with no history or current dispute. Ampe page written in Curio Class words from the Ghanaian sources under the frame's Base text; shown as one game children play in Ghana, not as all of Ghana; no child is asked to teach or explain their own culture. Social studies lean ssk-traditions (social studies K unit 5) is taught before. Sensitivity read: the Ampe sources first. Disclosure: health's steps (docs/courses/health/APPROACH.md, "If a student tells you something"): the school's reporting route and the counselor.

goal: Pairs play Ampe and say one way people play differently and one way the same, then rehearse "stand with them, tell a grown-up" for the left-out puppet.
note: Candidate kept: the Ampe version comes from a Ghanaian education source and the jumping stays on a marked spot. Movement: a cleared floor, walking feet, soft shoes, no pushing. Safety read: movement game.

goal: The class writes its "everyone can join" rule for one center and uses it in play; the teacher marks the first pairs on "stop, breathe, say what you want" from an unseen two-puppet card.
note: The teacher (or a teacher-held puppet) voices every pressure, dare, push or unkind line; no child plays the pushing, unkind or upset part.

goal: End of unit: the unseen two-puppet rehearsal for pairs not yet seen, the teacher playing the upset puppet, and a pictured page read aloud, one prompt per sub-skill (the refusal and the walk; stand with, tell; the fair rule; the right voice for a place; what a good leader does; taking turns in a team; one way a game from another place is different; one way it is the same).

goal: Hook: the question of how we stop and think before we choose; name and model the three pictured words, "stop, think, choose", with "if ___, then ___" on a picture case (running with scissors), two characters, one who rushes a puzzle and one who stops to think, and an "I wonder" question with "that is a new idea" for a classmate's.
note: Opening: the calm-down routine and "everyone can join" as retrieval. The stop-think-choose card is kept into grade 1. Three new sub-skills, each a one-step pictured phrase (Inside the 20 minutes). Disclosure: health's steps (docs/courses/health/APPROACH.md, "If a student tells you something"): the school's reporting route and the counselor.

goal: Pairs rehearse "stop, think, choose" and "if ___, then ___" on three picture cases until quick.
The second rehearsal session: pairs act the rushed and the careful puzzle on new cards and say which went better, then rehearse "I wonder" and "that is a new idea" in a circle.
note: The twelfth session of the unit (frame: a second Fluency for group 1).

goal: On a new story problem (a spilled box of crayons), pairs use "stop, think, choose", say what might happen next, ask one "I wonder" question and answer a partner's idea with "that is a new idea".

Model one fix for a small class problem in a story, picking a class game by counting picture votes ("we checked, more chose ___"), and sorting picture choices into "good for me and you" or "not" with one reason.
note: Math lean mk-sort-count (math K unit 2) is taught before. Votes count pictures, never children. RD6 uses everyday class choices (wash hands, share snack, push in line); health owns health topics. Core link: math:mk-sort-count, sorting and counting a class tally (the picture vote).

goal: Small groups rehearse acting one fix for a small problem, count a picture vote, and sort picture choices with a reason.
The class counts its own picture vote on which game to play and says "we checked, more chose ___"; pairs act a fix and sort two new choice pictures.
Model who a story choice touches on the "who does it touch?" circle, and one class goal with one step on the two-rung goal steps card, "my goal, one step".
note: Health K unit 2 (weeks 6 to 11) and PE K unit 6 (weeks 24 to 27) have had children pick one thing to work on; where the school runs them, SM4 opens with that pick as retrieval and the card adds the step (STANDARD section 7). Candidate kept: the class goal is chosen so it is tried on day 61 and checked on day 62, inside the unit.

goal: Pairs place three story choices on the "who does it touch?" circle, and the class tries its goal's one step.
The class checks its goal on the goal steps card and pairs place a new choice on the circle; the teacher marks the first pairs saying and showing "stop, think, choose" on an unseen scene card.

End of unit: a pictured page read aloud, one prompt per sub-skill (what happens next; which character thought first; the "I wonder" question; the fix; which group is bigger on a sorted tally; the good-for-us sort; who the choice touches; the goal's one step), and "stop, think, choose" on an unseen card for pairs not yet seen.

goal: Hook: the question of how a team works; model the talk turn card with one more step, listen and then reply on the same topic ("I agree with ___ because"), and small groups with a job each (holder, taper, checker) sharing ideas with the card.
note: Opening retrieval: the kindergarten talk turn card, "eyes look, wait my turn", and its block-tower turns. ELA lean ela:e1-discussion in the same weeks (ELA grade 1 unit 1). Leave-out bridge: if kindergarten unit 1 was left out, the first ten minutes teach the talk turn card's one-step form. Library places AASL.III.D.2 with RS4; grade 2 owns it. Disclosure: health's steps (docs/courses/health/APPROACH.md, "If a student tells you something"): the school's reporting route and the counselor.

goal: Pairs rehearse listen and reply with the talk turn card on three easy topics, and groups rehearse their job cards in a dry run.
Small groups build a paper bridge in one session with a job each, sharing ideas with listen and reply.
note: Candidate kept: the build is this one session so the rehearsal, not the build, is the point. Paper, tape, child-safe scissors only, at tables. Safety read: scissors and tape.

goal: Model "You were good at ___ when ___" told to a teammate after the bridge task, and one strength an invented teammate brings, then the team strengths poster.
note: Opening retrieval: kindergarten "I saw you ___" and the strengths page. The poster is optional; home languages and culture welcome when offered, never asked about.

goal: Pairs rehearse "You were good at ___ when ___" on picture cases of teammates, and children add one strength to the poster if they choose.
In a new group task (sorting the class library bin by picture), groups listen and reply and then tell a teammate what they were good at; the teacher marks the first groups on listen and reply.

End of unit: listen and reply watched in a short group task against the look-fors for groups not yet seen, and a pictured page read aloud, one prompt per sub-skill (the reply that stays on topic; each job in a team; the specific "good at" words; a teammate's strength).
Reteach the step most marked "not yet" and rehearse it again; send the family note (each person at a meal says one thing the person before them said).
note: Carry it out: "listen, then reply" at every class talk.

goal: Hook: the question of what I can do when a feeling gets big; model the calm-down card's grade 1 form, "stop, breathe" (the balloon breath), then count to five, with a choice of breathe or count; four more feeling words on the feelings faces chart with two clues (the face and what happened); and a character with a big frustrated feeling who uses "stop, breathe", picks what to do and hears how the other character felt.
note: Opening: kindergarten's calm-down steps; the feelings faces and the big-feeling choice are retrieved at the start of their own modeled steps. Calm-down first, then feelings, then the big feeling (frame order). Candidate kept: the count-to-five picture is drawn once for the shared card, so PE grade 1 unit 11 and health use the same picture. ELA lean ela:e1-feeling-sense-words: ELA grade 1 unit 2 opens in week 7, so the feeling words are taught here on the chart (frame bridge). goal: Pairs rehearse the calm-down routine, each choosing breathe or count, then name a character's feeling with two clues on picture cards.
On a new scene card (a lost game), pairs act the character's chosen calm-down tool and choice, and say how the other character felt.
note: Carry it out from here: a partner reminds with the cue word.

goal: Model getting back to work when a partner is chatting with "back to my work" said politely, two pictured steps to get ready (desk clear, tools out) checked on the goal steps card, and a class picture vote on one calm corner tool with why it helps others too.
note: Opening: kindergarten "eyes on my work"; "first, next", "I choose ___" and the goal steps card are retrieved at the start of their own modeled steps. Leave-out bridge: if kindergarten unit 6 was left out, the first ten minutes teach the goal steps card's one-step form. Library places AASL.V.D.1 with SM3; grade 2 owns it.

goal: Pairs rehearse "back to my work" with one partner playing a friendly chatter from a script card, and the get-ready steps until quick.
note: The chatter is friendly and scripted; no unkind part.
